A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MRGen research work. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices A–E are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original image-generation and segmentation experiments, reconstruction and conditioning ablations, in-domain generation results, and qualitative failure cases.

after.justification: v2 retains original generation and segmentation results and additionally reports annotation-quality verification and expanded baseline comparisons.

M1.justification: The autoencoder, text-conditioned diffusion model, mask controller, and training losses remain substantively unchanged. However, v2 Appendix B.3 adds a filtering fallback: when no candidate passes, thresholds are lowered by 0.10 and the highest-quality candidate is selected. v1 specifies rejection below fixed thresholds. This changes the stated selection procedure without establishing when it was implemented.

E1.justification: MedGen-1M becomes the MRI-only MRGen-DB: Radiopaedia-CT, AMOS22CT, and MSD-Liver are removed from the documented corpus. Tables 2–3 also lose three CT-to-MRI transfer scenarios. The five MRI datasets and ten MRI transfer directions remain, so the revision substantially narrows domain coverage rather than merely renaming the dataset.

E2.justification: v2 adds UNSB to the main generation and segmentation comparisons. Appendix Table 9 additionally evaluates MaskGAN, MAISI, few-shot nnUNet, UniVerSeg, and TotalSegmentator-MRI. SAM2, oracle-box, and target-supervised nnUNet references from v1 are retained for four MRI directions but disappear for six other retained MRI directions; their movement is therefore only partial.

E3.justification: v2 removes L1 reconstruction error and revises the reported PROMISE12 test size from 110 to 240 slices. New evaluations specify source pretraining followed by fine-tuning on 5% target annotations, and manual audits sampling approximately 5,000 region labels and 60 modality descriptions. Principal metrics, MRI split rows apart from that correction, and MRGen training budgets otherwise remain stable.

E4.justification: v2 adds a targeted manual audit of automatic annotations and briefly reports that data balancing did not materially affect performance. It removes the MRI-only versus CT-plus-MRI autoencoder control from v1 Table 7. The remaining reconstruction, text-conditioning, target-image, and autofilter ablations largely persist, as do the small-mask and false-negative failure cases.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, experimental seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or formal significance tests. The new annotation audit supplies point accuracies and sampling details, without introducing uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: v2 adds UNSB results, including mean FID 194.78, extended DSC comparisons in Table 9, and annotation accuracies of 95.33% and 91.67%. CT-transfer results, the MRI-only VAE control, and L1 results are removed. Corresponding MRI entries in Tables 2–3 retain identical values; MRGen's aggregate FID changes from 78.95 to 82.18 and nnUNet DSC from 43.43 to 44.71 because the evaluated scenario set shrinks, not because those entries improve.

T1.justification: Appendix A retains the diffusion equations and derivations, and the substantive mathematical objectives remain unchanged. The added cross-attention equation and block-indexed controller notation restate operations already described in v1; no new theorem, proof, or substantive mathematical argument appears.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains generating text-and-mask-conditioned MRI training data for modalities lacking target annotations. v2 narrows the dataset contribution to MRI and adds explicit, qualified priority claims for the first open-source dataset curated for medical image generation and the first general medical generative model tailored to annotation-scarce MRI.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations for MAISI's poor transfer through missing modality conditioning, qualifications about privileged annotations in reference methods, and an explicit computational explanation for restricting experiments to 2D slices. It removes the interpretation that additional CT training improves reconstruction. The main generation mechanism explanations and existing failure limitations largely persist.

D1.justification: New Appendix B.3 documents source-mask use across training and test partitions, the registered MSD-Prostate exception, separate T1 phase generation, filtering fallback, and per-scenario synthetic-data counts. v2 also discloses the 40% region-label confidence cutoff and additional baseline implementation settings. These materially improve experimental traceability, although v1's zero-convolution initialization detail disappears. Hardware, principal hyperparameters, and promised resource-access arrangements remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands positioning across medical generation, translation, and few-shot segmentation, adding works such as GenerateCT, UNSB, MaskGAN, UniVerSeg, RadImageGAN, and MedM2G. Its appendix distinguishes several comparator families and their annotation requirements. It also introduces explicit first-dataset/model claims while dropping the mask-controller section's direct ControlNet attribution, although that work remains cited elsewhere.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, and substantial portions of the method narrative are rewritten. Dataset curation moves inside the Method section, MedGen-1M is renamed throughout, generation ablations move into the main discussion, and the appendix is reorganized around synthetic-data documentation and broader comparisons.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is redrawn, qualitative grids are reorganized with UNSB columns and revised example placement, and the CT distribution graphic disappears. v1 Tables 7–8 are merged into v2 Table 4. New synthetic-data and comparison tables appear, with privileged reference methods shaded in Table 9. Appendix visualization grids are consolidated rather than simply renumbered.

improvement.justification: v2 adds useful comparator coverage, annotation verification, and substantial reproduction details. However, v1 Tables 7–8 describe CT-plus-MRI experiments, while v2 Table 4 retains their corresponding numerical values under an MRI-only training/evaluation description without explaining reruns or recalculation. SAM2 and oracle comparisons also disappear for six retained MRI scenarios. The documentation gains coexist with unresolved result provenance and reduced comparative context, preventing a reliable judgment of net overall improvement.
